question: In an economy, the modernisation goal of a five-year plan is concerned with:
solution:
The correct answer is __**New Technology**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Modernisation in a** five-year plan** refers to the adoption of **new technology** to improve productivity and efficiency across sectors in the economy.
 
• It involves replacing outdated or traditional technologies with advanced and innovative systems to meet global standards.
 
• This goal focuses on enhancing industrial output, agricultural practices, healthcare, and infrastructure through technological advancements.
 
• Modernisation is essential for achieving long-term economic growth and competitiveness in a globalised market.
 
• Examples include adopting renewable energy technologies, mechanised farming equipment, and digital transformation in governance and businesses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Five-Year Plans:**

 
 
• The Five-Year Plans were centralised and integrated national economic programs in India, starting from 1951.
 
• These plans aimed at achieving various objectives, including growth, self-reliance, modernisation, and equity.
 
• The Planning Commission was responsible for formulating and overseeing these plans until its replacement by NITI Aayog in 2015.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Technology in Economic Growth:**
 
 
• Technological advancements help in reducing production costs and increasing output.
 
• They enable innovation, improve quality, and foster competitiveness in domestic and international markets.
 
• Examples include Artificial Intelligence (AI), Internet of Things (IoT), and biotechnology.
 
 
 
• **Modernisation and Agriculture:**
 
 
• Modernisation in agriculture involves the use of hybrid seeds, irrigation systems, and mechanised equipment.
 
• It helps in increasing yield, reducing dependency on manual labour, and ensuring food security.
 
 
 
• **Challenges of Modernisation:**
 
 
• High costs of adopting new technology may lead to inequality between developed and underdeveloped regions.
 
• It requires skilled manpower, which necessitates investment in education and training.
 
• Environmental concerns arise due to industrialisation and energy usage.
